extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) is a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research. The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish). The dataset also includes Language Models (LM) and baseline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models for all languages.
extraction.license: Public domain (LibriVox and Project Gutenberg data released in the public domain)
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
extraction.inLanguage: English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish
extraction.citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411v2 [eess.AS], December 2020.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. Audio data was downloaded using data preparation tools from the LibriLight open source library. All audio data is downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Acoustic models were trained on in-house datasets consisting of videos publicly shared by users (audio only, completely de-identified) to generate pseudo-labels. Text sources for audiobooks were downloaded from multiple domains including gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org, using automated parsers and manual approaches.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For some audiobooks, text sources were not available due to invalid links or incorrect page redirects. For example, all text sources from the spiegel.de domain (accounting for 1/3 of German audio data) were being redirected to invalid pages. Manual searches were conducted to find alternate sources. Some books were removed due to corrupted metadata such as missing title or speaker/author information.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks from LibriVox (https://librivox.org), with corresponding text from Project Gutenberg (http://www.gutenberg.org) and other online sources including archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, projekt-gutenberg.de, zeno.org, and spiegel.de.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Numbers in the matched text from books were replaced with the corresponding aligned words from pseudo labels to handle ambiguous number pronunciations. Heuristics were used to handle hyphens and apostrophes appearing unexpectedly in transcripts.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with TDS Convolutions and ASG loss. Pseudo labels were generated using beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model. Transcript retrieval was performed by matching pseudo labels to source text using TF-IDF similarity on bigrams and Smith-Waterman alignment. Candidate transcripts with WER > 40% between candidate transcript and pseudo label were filtered out. Dataset was split into train, development, and test sets with no speaker overlap, gender-balanced dev/test sets. Limited supervision datasets (10-hour, 1-hour, and six 10-minute sets) were also created.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters (punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols), removal of end-of-line hyphens, and filtering of characters outside valid unicode ranges for each language. Books with corrupted metadata, multiple speakers, or duplicate versions were removed. Audio segments with multiple speakers (e.g., 'Dramatic Reading') were excluded. For language model data, books with title edit distance less than 2 from dev/test set books were removed, and books sharing more than 1% of 5-grams with dev/test sets were also removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts for development and test sets were human-verified. Human transcribers listened to audio files while reading the generated transcript and were asked to correct only 'clear and obvious' errors to avoid introducing bias. Examples of corrections include diacritic corrections, missing words, and missing apostrophes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: WER between generated transcript (GT) and human rated transcript (HRT) was measured for dev and test sets across all 8 languages. WER ranged from 1.93% (Spanish dev) to 12.64% (Portuguese dev), indicating varying levels of transcript quality across languages.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: wav2letter@anywhere framework for streaming inference; TDS Convolutions with ASG loss for audio segmentation; beam-search decoding with 4-gram language model for pseudo label generation; TF-IDF similarity on bigrams for document retrieval; Smith-Waterman alignment for transcript matching; SVM with RBF kernel for gender classification; KenLM toolkit for language model training; pdftotext for extracting text from PDF/EPUB books
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is made freely available at http://www.openslr.org. Pretrained models and recipes are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/wav2letter. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker gender is labeled using a gender classifier (SVM with RBF kernel). Speaker identity information is included (speaker IDs). In-house training data used for acoustic models consists of de-identified audio from publicly shared videos.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to open new avenues in ASR and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research by providing a large, freely available multilingual speech corpus. It aims to promote open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and multilingual ASR, and can be extended for TTS research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks, which may not represent conversational or spontaneous speech. English is heavily dominant with 44.5K hours compared to approximately 6K hours total for all other languages. Speaker gender balance is enforced in development and test sets but not necessarily in training sets. The gender classifier used has accuracy of 95-96% and may introduce some labeling errors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is read-speech only and may not generalize to conversational or spontaneous speech. Polish has a high OOV rate of 13.39% in the language model, negatively impacting LM-based decoding. Some audiobooks could not be included due to unavailable or invalid text sources. The dataset may not cover all dialects or accents within each language.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems; multilingual ASR research; Text-to-Speech (TTS) research; low-resource ASR benchmarking using limited supervision sets (10-hour, 1-hour, 10-minute splits); language model training and evaluation.
